title: Perfect tensor tests detect upper bounds on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions and $R\Gamma$ uses K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. A perfect object is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Quasi-compact means every open cover of the point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Suppose that for every perfect $P$ there is an integer $b_P$ with $H^i(R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}K))=0$ for $i>b_P$. Then there is an integer $b$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$. No uniform bound on the different tests is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, proposition-detecting-bounded-above, implication (7)(b) to (1), with the perfect generator supplied by theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh.

proof.text: For any quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space $W$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, perfect $Q$ on $W$, and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$, ringed-site perfect duality and the all-degree global-Hom identification give $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,E[i])\cong H^i(R\Gamma(W,Q^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}E))$, with $Q^\vee$ perfect. Here global Hom is $R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom$, and the cited global-Hom statement identifies its degree-$i$ cohomology with morphisms to $E[i]$ without boundedness hypotheses. Apply the tensor-test assumption to $P=Q^\vee$. Thus the original $K$ satisfies $B_X(K)$, where $B_W(E)$ means: for each perfect $Q$ on $W$, $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,E[i])=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$, with the threshold allowed to depend on $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, equivalence of (2)-(6) with the perfect tests; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JJ lemma-dual-perfect-complex and section-global-RHom.

proof.text: Apply distinguished-square induction to the isomorphism-invariant property $T(W)$: every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$ satisfying $B_W(E)$ is bounded above. This is a property of every quasi-compact quasi-separated etale $W\to X$, not merely of the restriction of the fixed $K$. If $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, use the perfect test $Q=\mathcal O_W[0]$. The identity in Step 1, with $Q^\vee=\mathcal O_W[0]$, says $R\Gamma(W,E)$ is bounded above. The affine etale module equivalence has quasi-inverse $R\Gamma$, is exact and faithful, and satisfies $\mathcal H^i(a_BM)\cong a_B(H^iM)$. Writing $E\cong a_BM$, it follows that $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ above the same bound. This proves the affine base case, including $B=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, affine base case; Tag 08GP lemma-induction-principle; Tag 071Q lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site.

proof.text: For the induction step take an elementary distinguished square $(i:U\hookrightarrow W,p:V\to W)$ with $W$ quasi-compact quasi-separated, $U$ quasi-compact and $V$ affine, and assume $T(U),T(V),T(U\times_WV)$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$ satisfy $B_W(E)$. The supported Koszul high-localization node supplies a perfect $C_W=Rp_*B$ from a finite principal-open presentation of $U\times_WV$ in $V$. Since this particular test is perfect, $B_W(E)$ gives its required high-degree Hom vanishing. Hence for some integer $a$ the actual open unit induces $\tau_{\ge a}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\ge a}F$, where $F=Ri_*(i^*E)$. Exact etale restriction gives $i^*E$ quasi-coherent. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $i$ follow from the permanence lemma applied to $U,W$; consequently the direct-image theorem gives $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, supported Koszul construction and high-truncation comparison; Tag 08FA lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image (1).

proof.text: Fix a perfect $Q$ on $W$ and choose its Ext window $[c,d]$. For either $M=E$ or $M=F$, put $L=\tau_{<a}M$. For $i\ge a-c$ and $q\in[c,d]$, $q+i\ge a$, so $\mathcal H^q(L[i])=\mathcal H^{q+i}(L)=0$, and likewise for $L[i+1]$. The window lemma therefore makes both $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,L[i])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,L[i+1])$ zero. Apply representable exactness to the truncation triangle $L\to M\to\tau_{\ge a}M\to L[1]$ (and its rotation): $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,M[i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q,(\tau_{\ge a}M)[i])$. The isomorphism of Step 3 now shows that $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,F[i])=0$ for sufficiently large $i$. This is the two-line truncation argument of Tag 0GFF, written out using the existing window and triangle nodes; no uniform bound in $Q$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0GFF lemma-bounded-truncation, proof; used twice in the proof of Tag 0GFH.

proof.text: Let $R$ be any perfect object on $U$. The open-retract theorem gives a perfect $Q$ on $W$ and maps $R\xrightarrow{s}i^*Q\xrightarrow{r}R$ with $rs=1$. The canonical derived adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_U(i^*Q,i^*E[i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q,F[i])$, which is zero in high degrees by Step 4. For any $h:R\to i^*E[i]$, the composite $hr:i^*Q\to i^*E[i]$ is then zero and $h=(hr)s=0$. Thus $B_U(i^*E)$ holds. This uses the retract statement itself, not the proof or a generator theorem; it transfers each perfect test separately.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, open-generator restriction argument; Tag 09IX lemma-direct-summand-of-a-restriction. The all-perfect-tests version avoids choosing a single generator.

proof.text: By the induction hypothesis $T(U)$ and Step 5 there is $b_U$ with $\mathcal H^q(i^*E)=0$ for $q>b_U$. Apply the upper-bound theorem to $i:U\to W$: both spaces are quasi-compact, $W$ is quasi-separated, and $i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated as checked in Step 3. For some $N\ge1$, $\mathcal H^m(F)=0$ for $m\ge b_U+N$. Set $b=\max(a-1,b_U+N-1)$. If $m>b$, then $m\ge a$ and the high-truncation isomorphism of Step 3 identifies $\mathcal H^m(E)$ with $\mathcal H^m(F)=0$. This proves $T(W)$ and completes the distinguished-square step (only $T(U)$ is needed among the three induction hypotheses). The induction principle yields $T(X)$; Step 1 supplies $B_X(K)$, so $K$ has the required upper bound.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GFH proposition-detecting-bounded-above, distinguished-square proof; follows its Koszul and truncation argument, transferring all perfect tests via 09IX instead of selecting a generator.
